newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak cbank official says Forex move internal.
newsitem.headline: Slovak cbank official says Forex move internal.

text.p: A senior official at the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Friday said a measure presented to the central bank board, passed later in the day, should not greatly effect commercial banks.

Frantisek Szulenyi, NBS Treasury Department Director who participated in the creation of the "risk management and open foreign exchange position" measure, told Reuters the measure had been presented for approval mainly as a technical move.
"The measure, as we prepared it for the governing board's approval, is only for our internal position, for automating the manual monitoring of forex positions we do on a daily basis," Szulenyi said.
"It has nothing to do with commercial banks at all."
But he added that he was not aware of the measure's final version approved on Friday. Board officials were not immediately available for comment.

Interbank money market dealers had said they were eyeing the NBS for a possible repo rate cut or some other measures effecting rates after Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said this week that measures were being taken to lower rates.
The government also appointed former deputy finance minister Jozef Magula this week to the bank board, which had made analysts wary of possible policy changes at the meeting.

The NBS's board said it had approved a "practical framework" for the measure at its regular meeting, creating conditions for an automated system of data processing necessary for risk management within an open foreign exchange position.
The NBS will operate using the system from April 30.

Sylvia Majlingova, Liquidity Department Director at CSOB, told Reuters the forex risk measure may contribute to an interest rate decline, for example, by implementing crown position limits for banks. "But we have no idea what the measure means at the moment," she said.
